# MIOSA CLI 1.1.18

Supersedes 1.1.17, which was tagged and release-noted on 2026-08-23 but never
reached npm, so no user ever received it. Every 1.1.17 change is included below
and nothing from it is dropped. The last version on npm is 1.1.16.

## Added

- `miosa templates update <id> --dockerfile <path>` updates an existing template. While the template has no usable image its stored Dockerfile is replaced in place, keeping the same ID and name; once it has one, the new Dockerfile is built as a new build instead. The command states which of the two happened.
- `miosa templates rebuild <id>` starts a new build of an existing template, optionally from a different Dockerfile.
- `miosa templates list` gained a `SOURCE` column, a `USABLE` column, and `--mine`, `--built-in` and `--verify` filters. Your own templates are listed first.
- `miosa templates create` and `get` report `Exists` and `Usable` as separate facts, with the reason a template is not yet usable.
- Carried forward from 1.1.17: an explicit `--static` deploy mode that omits build and run commands for static sites.

## Fixed

- Field-level validation errors are now printed as one legible line per field instead of dumping the raw JSON response body. A duplicate template name reads as a name collision against `--name`, and the CLI no longer repeats a server-side misattribution: a uniqueness error blamed on a field the request never sent is reported as a duplicate, with a note, rather than as the caller's input.
- Unreachable API endpoints now name the host, which configuration value set it (`MIOSA_ENDPOINT`, `~/.miosa/config.json`, or the built-in default), and the exact command that changes it. DNS failures, refused connections, timeouts and TLS failures are distinguished. An endpoint that is not an absolute http(s) URL is rejected up front instead of surfacing as `Invalid URL`.
- Server-sent event streams no longer lose frames. Frame state is kept across chunk boundaries, so an event split by the transport is delivered instead of dropped, and its `event:` name is preserved rather than discarded. Multi-byte characters split across chunks, CRLF terminators, comment frames and an unterminated final frame are all handled.
- `miosa templates builds` shows build failures. It read a field the API does not send, so the ERROR column was always empty.
- `miosa db logs --follow` now sends the same tenant and workspace scope headers as every other command; it previously resolved against the API key's default scope.
- A 406 response is reported as a server-side content negotiation fault rather than a bare `HTTP 406`.
- Every `templates` subcommand honours `--json` on failure.
- Carried forward from 1.1.17: `miosa deploy --docker-deploy` is automation-safe, so JSON mode and non-TTY stdin never open interactive prompts.
- Carried forward from 1.1.17: unknown project shapes fail before reaching the API and require explicit `--build-command` and `--run-command` instead of guessing.
- Carried forward from 1.1.17: creation flags (`--name`, `--branch`, `--build-command`, `--run-command`, `--static`) passed when `.miosa.json` already exists are an error, so automation never silently redeploys a different configuration.

## Removed

- Dropped the widened `Accept` header and bespoke 406 message on the database log stream. That was a workaround for a route that sat behind a JSON-only pipeline; the route is now served without content negotiation, and the workaround only converted a misconfiguration into silent empty output.
